fullPassage: Viruses are the freeloading vampires of the body. Not a plant, animal, or bacterium, these infectious agents are unable to live on their own. Instead, they take over other cells to help them reproduce and carry out metabolic activities. First identified in 1892 by the Russian scientist Dmitry I. Ivanovsky, viruses get their name from the Latin word meaning "poison" and "slimy liquid." Today, scientists have identified more than 5,000 different types of viruses. Some of them, such as those that cause the common cold and flu, multiply rapidly and kill the host cell, while others, such as the genital herpes virus, can remain inactive in the body for years. Still others, such as the one that leads to AIDS, are slow viruses, meaning that they remain in the cells and reproduce slowly over years. Essentially, viruses consist of nucleic acids - either DNA or RNA - surrounded by a protein shell. Most viruses are shaped as either rods or spherical, 20-sided figures. Because they lack enzymes for energy production and ribosomes for protein synthesis and reproduction, viruses attach to a host cell. Like a needle, they inject their genetic material into the new cell. At that point, the viral nucleic acid takes over the cellular machinery, producing new virus particles. Often, this process destroys the host cell. This releases new viruses to infect other cells. Because viruses are stuck in the cells, they're much more difficult to kill than bacteria. Some antiviral medications attack viruses, while vaccines are also effective in stimulating the immune system to produce white blood cells that target specific viruses.

❌ ① unable — are unable to live: 바이러스는 스스로 살 수 '없다'는 맥락이라 적절해요.

❌ ② multiply — multiply rapidly: 빠르게 '증식한다'는 맥락이라 적절해요.

✅ ③ heal — 원문은 kill. 감기·독감 바이러스는 빠르게 증식하며 숙주 세포를 '죽인다(kill)'는 흐름이에요. heal(치유하다)을 넣으면 '세포를 치유한다'가 되어 뒤의 '느린 바이러스는 잠복한다'는 대조와 맞지 않아요 ←정답

❌ ④ immune — the immune system: 백신이 자극하는 '면역' 체계라 적절해요.
det.tip: multiply rapidly and kill the host cell(죽이다) ↔ heal(치유하다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 앞 'Because viruses are stuck in the cells(세포 안에 갇혀 있어서)'가 이유이므로, 바이러스는 박테리아보다 '죽이기 어렵다(difficult to kill)'가 되어야 함.

questions.passage: Viruses are the freeloading vampires of the body. Not a plant, animal, or bacterium, these infectious agents are unable to live on their own. Instead, they take over other cells to help them reproduce and carry out metabolic activities. First identified in 1892 by the Russian scientist Dmitry I. Ivanovsky, viruses get their name from the Latin word meaning "poison" and "slimy liquid." Today, scientists have identified more than 5,000 different types of viruses. Some of them, such as those that cause the common cold and flu, multiply rapidly and kill the host cell, while others, such as the genital herpes virus, can remain inactive in the body for years. Still others, such as the one that leads to AIDS, are slow viruses, meaning that they remain in the cells and reproduce slowly over years. Essentially, viruses consist of nucleic acids - either DNA or RNA - surrounded by a protein shell. Most viruses are shaped as either rods or spherical, 20-sided figures. Because they lack enzymes for energy production and ribosomes for protein synthesis and reproduction, viruses attach to a host cell. Like a needle, they inject their genetic material into the new cell. At that point, the viral nucleic acid takes over the cellular machinery, producing new virus particles. Often, this process destroys the host cell. This releases new viruses to infect other cells. Because viruses are stuck in the cells, they're much more difficult to kill than bacteria. Some antiviral medications attack viruses, while vaccines are also effective in stimulating the immune system to produce white blood cells that target specific viruses.

[조건] (1) cell, genetic, inject, into, material, new, the, their, they 를 모두 사용

det.korean: '주입한다'가 핵심 동사. 주어 they + 동사 inject + 목적어 their genetic material + 방향 into the new cell.

단계별로: 주어 they(그것들) → 동사 inject(주입한다) → 무엇을? their genetic material(자신의 유전 물질) → 어디로? into the new cell(새로운 세포 안으로).

그래서 'they inject their genetic material into the new cell'(정확히 9단어)가 돼요. into가 '~안으로'라는 방향을 나타내요.

"그것들은 자신들이 번식하고 물질대사 활동을 수행하도록 돕기 위해 다른 세포를 장악한다."

[조건] (1) activities, and, carry, cells, help, metabolic, other, out, over, reproduce, take, them, they, to 를 모두 사용
       (2) 정확히 14단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '~하도록 돕기 위해'는 to help + 목적어 + 동사원형. help them 뒤에 reproduce와 carry out을 and로 병렬 연결한다.
det.analysis:
핵심은 두 가지예요. ① 목적을 나타내는 to부정사(to help ~하기 위해), ② help + 목적어 + 동사원형.

단계별로: 주어 they → 동사 take over(장악한다) → 목적어 other cells → 목적 'to help them(그것들이 …하도록 돕기 위해)' → help them 뒤에는 동사원형 reproduce, 그리고 and로 carry out을 병렬로 이어요 → 무엇을? metabolic activities.

그래서 'they take over other cells to help them reproduce and carry out metabolic activities'(정확히 14단어)가 돼요. help 뒤의 reproduce와 carry out이 to 없이 동사원형으로 나란히 오는 점이 핵심이에요.
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형(reproduce and carry out): 병렬

questions.wa: they take over other cells to help them reproduce and carry out metabolic activities
accept: they take over other cells to help them reproduce and carry out metabolic activities
they take over other cells to help them carry out metabolic activities and reproduce

questions.passage: Viruses are the freeloading vampires of the body. Not a plant, animal, or bacterium, these infectious agents are unable to live on their own. Instead, they take over other cells to help them reproduce and carry out metabolic activities. First identified in 1892 by the Russian scientist Dmitry I. Ivanovsky, viruses get their name from the Latin word meaning "poison" and "slimy liquid." Today, scientists have identified more than 5,000 different types of viruses. Some of them, such as those that cause the common cold and flu, multiply rapidly and kill the host cell, while others, such as the genital herpes virus, can remain inactive in the body for years. Still others, such as the one that leads to AIDS, are slow viruses, meaning that they remain in the cells and reproduce slowly over years. Essentially, viruses consist of nucleic acids - either DNA or RNA - surrounded by a protein shell. Most viruses are shaped as either rods or spherical, 20-sided figures. Because they lack enzymes for energy production and ribosomes for protein synthesis and reproduction, viruses attach to a host cell. Like a needle, they inject their genetic material into the new cell. At that point, the viral nucleic acid takes over the cellular machinery, producing new virus particles. Often, this process destroys the host cell. __________. Because viruses are stuck in the cells, they're much more difficult to kill than bacteria. Some antiviral medications attack viruses, while vaccines are also effective in stimulating the immune system to produce white blood cells that target specific viruses.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (영어로, 8단어)

[ cells / infect / new / other / releases / This / to / viruses ]

det.korean: 주어 This(단수) + 동사 releases + 목적어 new viruses + 목적의 to부정사 to infect other cells.
det.analysis:
주어부터 잡아요: This(이것)가 주어예요. 단수라서 동사는 releases(방출한다)예요.

무엇을 방출하나요? new viruses(새로운 바이러스). 그리고 '왜/무엇을 위해'를 나타내는 to부정사 to infect other cells(다른 세포를 감염시키기 위해)를 붙여요.

그래서 'This releases new viruses to infect other cells'(8단어)가 완성돼요. 단수 주어 This에 releases가 오는 점을 기억하세요.
det.tip: This(단수) + releases + to부정사(목적)

questions.wa: This releases new viruses to infect other cells
accept: This releases new viruses to infect other cells

Some of them, such as those that cause the common cold and flu, multiply rapidly and kill the host cell, while others, such as the genital herpes virus, can remain inactive in the body for years. questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.

"그것들은 세포 안에 머무르며 수년에 걸쳐 천천히 증식한다."

[조건] (1) and, cells, in, over, reproduce, remain, slowly, the, they, years 를 모두 사용
       (2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 동사 두 개(remain, reproduce)를 and로 병렬 연결. remain in the cells와 reproduce slowly over years.
det.analysis:
주어 they 뒤에 동사 두 개가 and로 이어져요.

단계별로: they → remain in the cells(세포 안에 머무른다) → and → reproduce(증식한다) → slowly(천천히) → over years(수년에 걸쳐).

그래서 'they remain in the cells and reproduce slowly over years'(정확히 10단어)가 돼요. remain과 reproduce가 and로 나란히 연결되는 병렬 구조가 핵심이에요.
det.tip: remain ... and reproduce: 동사 병렬

questions.wa: they remain in the cells and reproduce slowly over years
accept: they remain in the cells and reproduce slowly over years
they reproduce slowly over years and remain in the cells
